# @ic-reactor/parser

> A Candid parser compiled from Rust to WebAssembly. It validates Candid
> source, turns it into JavaScript IDL factories and TypeScript declarations,
> describes its types and methods, and checks upgrade compatibility.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/parser` 0.5.0.

Read this file from `node_modules/@ic-reactor/parser/llms.txt` when writing
code against the installed version. The complete guide for every package is
https://ic-reactor.b3pay.net/llms-full.txt, and behaviour changes are in
https://github.com/B3Pay/ic-reactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/parser
```

Most apps do not install it directly: `@ic-reactor/candid` depends on it and
loads it when it parses, and `@ic-reactor/codegen` (behind the CLI and the Vite
plugin) uses it to write declarations.

## Setup and Usage

```ts
import init, {
  didToJs,
  didToTs,
  parseDid,
  validateIDL,
} from "@ic-reactor/parser"

const candid = `service : {
  greet : (text) -> (text) query;
  set_greeting : (text) -> ();
}`

await init() // required on the web build (browsers, bundlers); a no-op on Node

try {
  validateIDL(candid) // true, or throws the parser's message as a string
} catch (message) {
  throw new Error(`Invalid Candid: ${String(message)}`)
}

for (const method of parseDid(candid).service?.methods ?? []) {
  console.log(method.name, method.mode) // "greet query", "set_greeting update"
}

const js = didToJs(candid) // JavaScript source exporting idlFactory and init
const dts = didToTs(candid) // TypeScript declarations with interface _SERVICE
console.log(js, dts)
```

## When to Use What

| Need                                                 | Use                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Check that Candid source parses and type-checks      | `validateIDL(source)` inside `try` / `catch`       |
| JavaScript `idlFactory` source for a `.did`          | `didToJs(source)`                                  |
| TypeScript declarations (`_SERVICE`) for a `.did`    | `didToTs(source)`                                  |
| Types and methods as data (names, modes, arguments)  | `parseDid(source)`                                 |
| Is a new interface a safe upgrade of the old one     | `verifyCompatibility(oldDid, newDid)`              |
| Call a canister whose Candid you fetched at run time | `@ic-reactor/candid` (it runs this parser for you) |
| Generate files from `.did` in a project              | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` or `@ic-reactor/cli`     |

## Details

- One entrypoint, `@ic-reactor/parser`. Export conditions pick the build:
  `browser`, `workerd` and the default resolve to the web build, which needs
  `await init()` (or `initSync(module)`) before any other call; `node`
  resolves to the Node build, which initializes itself.
- `didToJs` and `didToTs` return source strings, not modules.
- Invalid Candid throws the parser's message as a string. An input the parser
  itself fails on throws an `Error` with the original as `cause`, and later
  calls keep working.
- A record field or variant tag whose name looks like a numeric id (`_0_`) is
  printed under the hash of its name (`_4735054_`), and `parseDid` names it the
  same way, because that is the field a canister expects. A hand-written
  `.did` that spells a Motoko numeric field `_0_` must write `0`.
- A Candid type named `_SERVICE`, like a TypeScript type keyword (`string`,
  `number`, `bigint`, `symbol`, `object`, `any`, `unknown`, `never`,
  `undefined`) or like a type operator (`keyof`, `readonly`, `unique`,
  `infer`) is renamed with `_` appended (`string_`).
- Candid imports cannot be resolved from one source string: every function
  throws for `import service "file.did"`, and a plain `import` is ignored.
- `verifyCompatability(a, b)` is deprecated;
  `verifyCompatibility(oldDid, newDid)` takes the old interface first and
  returns `false` instead of throwing for an incompatible upgrade.

## Do Not

- Call a function on the web build before `await init()`.
- Import `@ic-reactor/parser/web`, `/nodejs` or `/bundler`, or deep-import
  `dist/`: there is only the `.` entry.
- Expect `validateIDL` to return `false`; catch what it throws.
- Rename the hashed or suffixed names in generated declarations by hand.
